title: The Pipeline Deployed, But the Old Code Is Still Running
intro: The deploy pipeline is green and says it deployed the fix for the login bug. Users still hit the bug. Half the pods seem fixed, half don't.

steps.prompt: Check which image the deployment's pods are configured to run.
The tag is ':latest'. Check the actual image digest each running pod is using.
steps.fake_output:
web-7f9d-a1b2	acme/web@sha256:9a8b...  (new)
web-7f9d-c3d4	acme/web@sha256:1f2e...  (old)
web-7f9d-e5f6	acme/web@sha256:1f2e...  (old)
steps.hint: Same tag, different digests — the tag points at different content on different nodes.

steps.prompt: Check the pull policy that decides whether nodes re-download ':latest'.
steps.hint: IfNotPresent means a node that already has 'acme/web:latest' cached never pulls the new one.

steps.prompt: Deploy the fix by an immutable tag — the pipeline builds acme/web:3f9a2c1 (the commit SHA).
steps.hint: A unique tag per build forces every node to pull the exact image.

steps.prompt: Confirm the rollout completes on every pod.
steps.hint: Verify all pods moved to the new image.

resolution: The pipeline pushed a new image to the same mutable ':latest' tag. Because the pod spec didn't change (still 'acme/web:latest'), Kubernetes had no reason to roll anything; pods restarted for other reasons landed on nodes where IfNotPresent reused whatever ':latest' was cached — sometimes new, sometimes weeks old. The result was a fleet running a random mix of versions, with a green pipeline hiding it. The fix is immutable tags: tag every image with the git commit SHA (or a version), deploy by that tag, and never reuse a tag for different content. It also makes rollbacks meaningful — 'roll back to 3f9a2c0' names an exact artifact, while 'roll back to latest' means nothing.
